purpose: Hydroxyzine is used to help relieve anxiety and tension, and it can also help you feel calm enough to fall asleep. It is also used to treat itching caused by allergies or skin reactions. Sometimes doctors prescribe it to help you relax before a medical procedure or surgery.
how_it_works: Hydroxyzine works by blocking certain natural chemicals in your brain and body called histamines and other receptors that cause anxiety, itching, and alertness. By blocking these signals, it helps calm your nervous system down so you feel more relaxed and less anxious. Think of it like a dimmer switch for your brain's stress and itch responses.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is feeling drowsy or sleepy, which is actually helpful if it is being used for sleep or anxiety. You may also notice a dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, or an upset stomach. These effects are usually mild and get better as your body adjusts.
warnings: Because hydroxyzine causes drowsiness, you should not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires full alertness until you know how it affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication since it can make the drowsiness much worse. Tell your doctor if you have heart rhythm problems, liver disease, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as special precautions may be needed.
typical_dosing: For anxiety in adults, the usual dose is 25 to 100 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. For sleep, a typical dose is 50 to 100 mg taken at bedtime. For itching, doses may be lower and adjusted based on your needs. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed and do not take more than directed.
